message.content:
**Kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from a Windows command prompt**

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

- `/IM code.exe` – target the executable name (`code.exe` is the VS Code process).
- `/F` – force‑terminate the process (no graceful shutdown).

---

### Optional variations

| Option | What it does | Example |
|--------|--------------|---------|
| `/T` | Also terminate any child processes spawned by the target. | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |
| `/PID <pid>` | Target a specific process ID instead of the image name. | `taskkill /PID 1234 /F` |
| `/FI "<filter>"` | Filter which processes to kill (e.g., by username, session, memory usage). | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq <user>"` |

---

### PowerShell alternative

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

This does the same thing but uses PowerShell’s cmdlets.

---

### Quick one‑liner to kill *all* VS Code instances

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

That will close every `code.exe` process and any child processes it may have spawned.
